source_text: Καὶ ὅτι διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ ὑμῶν καὶ διὰ τὰς εἰδωλολατρείας, ἀλλ᾿ οὐ διὰ τὸ ἐνδεὴς εἶναι τῶν τοιούτων προσφορῶν, ἐνετείλατο ὁμοίως ταῦτα γίνεσθαι, ἀκούσατε πῶς περὶ τούτων λέγει διὰ Ἀμώς, ἑνὸς τῶν δώδεκα, βοῶν· Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐπιθυμοῦντες τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ κυρίου. Ἵνα τί αὕτη ὑμῖν ἡ ἡμέρα κυρίου: Καὶ αὐτή ἐστι σκότος καὶ οὐ φῶς. Ὅν τρόπον ὅταν ἐκφύγῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ λέοντος, καὶ συναντήσῃ αὐτῷ ἡ ἄρκτος, καὶ εἰσπηδήσῃ εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπερείσηται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν τοῖχον, καὶ δάκῃ αὐτὸν ὁ ὄφις. Οὐχὶ σκότος ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου καὶ οὐ φῶς, καὶ γνόφος οὐκ ἔχων φέγγος αὐτῆς; Μεμίσηκα, ἀπῶσμαι τὰς ἑορτὰς ὑμῶν, καὶ οὐ μὴ ὀσφρανθῶ ἐν ταῖς πανηγύρεσιν ὑμῶν. Διότι ἐὰν ἐνέγκητέ μοι τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ τὰς θυσίας ὑμῶν, οὐ προσδέξομαι αὐτὰ καὶ σωτηρίου ἐπιφανείας ὑμῶν οὐκ ἐπιβλέψομαι. Ἀπόστησον ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ πλῆθος ᾠδῶν σου καὶ ψαλμῶν· ὀργάνων σου οὐκ ἀκούσομαι. Καὶ κυλισθήσεται ὡς ὕδωρ κρίμα καὶ ἡ δικαιοσύνη ὡς χειμάρρους ἄβατος. Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ; λέγει κύριος. Καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν Ῥαφάν, τοὺς τύπους, οὓς ἐποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς. Καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Δαμασκοῦ, λέγει κύριος· ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὄνομα αὐτῷ. Οὐαὶ οἱ κατασπαταλῶντες Σιὼν καὶ τοῖς πεποιθόσιν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σαμαρείας. Οἱ ὠνομασμένοι ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀρχηγοῖς ἀπετρύγησαν ἀρχὰς ἐθνῶν· εἰσῆλθον ἑαυτοῖς οἶκος Ἰσραήλ. Διάβητε πάντες εἰς Χαλάνην καὶ ἴδετε, καὶ πορεύθητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Ἀμὰθ τὴν μεγάλην, καὶ κατάβητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Γὲθ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, τὰς κρατίστας ἐκ πασῶν τῶν βασιλειῶν τούτων, εἰ πλείονά ἐστι τὰ ὅρια αὐτῶν τῶν ὁρίων ὑμῶν. Οἱ ἐρχόμενοι εἰς ἡμέραν πονηράν, οἱ ἐγγίζοντες καὶ ἐφαπτόμενοι σαββάτων ψευδῶν, οἱ κοιμώμενοι ἐπὶ κλινῶν ἐλεφαντίνων καὶ κατασπαταλῶντες ἐπὶ ταῖς στρωμναῖς αὐτῶν, οἱ ἐσθίοντες ἄρνας ἐκ ποιμνίων καὶ μοσχάρια ἐκ μέσου βουκολίων γαλαθηνά, οἱ ἐπικροτοῦντες πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τῶν ὀργάνων, ὡς ἑστῶτα ἐλογίσαντο καὶ οὐχ ὡς φεύγοντα, οἱ πίνοντες ἐν φιάλαις οἶνον καὶ τὰ πρῶτα μύρα χριόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ἔπασχον οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῇ συντριβῇ τοῦ Ἰωσήφ. Διὰ τοῦτο νῦν αἰχμάλωτοι ἔσονται ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς δυναστῶν τῶν ἀποικιζομένων, καὶ μεταστραφήσεται οἴκημα κακούργων, καὶ ἐξαρθήσεται χρεμετισμὸς ἵππων ἐξ Ἐφραΐμ . Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ἱερεμίου· Συναγάγετε τὰ κρέα ὑμῶν καὶ τὰς θυσίας καὶ φάγετε, ὅτι οὔτε περὶ θυσιῶν ἢ σπονδῶν ἐνετειλάμην τοῖς πατράσιν ὑμῶν, ῄ ἡμέρᾳ ἐπελαβόμην τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου [JÉR., VII, 21-22]. Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Δαυΐδ ἐν τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ οὕτως ἔφη· Θεὸς θεῶν κύριος ἐλάλησε, καὶ ἐκάλεσε τὴν γῆν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν ἡλίου μέχρι δυσμῶν. Ἐκ Σιὼν ἡ εὐπρέπεια τῆς ὡραιότητος αὐτοῦ. Ὁ θεὸς ἐμφανῶς ἥξει, ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, καὶ οὐ παρασιωπήσεται· πῦρ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ καυθήσεται, καὶ κύκλῳ αὐτοῦ καταιγὶς σφόδρα. Προσκαλέσεται τὸν οὐρανὸν ἂνω καὶ τὴν γῆν τοῦ διακρῖναι τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ. Συναγάγετε αὐτῷ τοὺς ὁσίους αὐτοῦ, τοὺς διατιθεμένους τὴν διαθήκην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ θυσίαις. Καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσιν οἱ οὐρανοὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, ὅτι θεὸς κριτής ἐστιν. Ἄκουσον, λαός μου, καὶ λαλήσω σοι, Ἰσραήλ, καὶ διαμαρτυροῦμαί σοι· ὁ θεός, ὁ θεός σου εἰμὶ ἐγώ. Οὐκ ἐπὶ ταῖς θυσίαις σου ἐλέγξω σε· τὰ δὲ ὁλοκαυτώματά σου ἐνώπιόν μου ἐστὶ διὰ παντός. Οὐ δέξομαι ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου σου μόσχους οὐδὲ ἐκ τῶν ποιμνίων σου χιμάρους, ὅτι ἐμά ἐστι πάντα τὰ θηρία τοῦ ἀγροῦ, κτήνη ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι καὶ βόες· ἔγνωκα πάντα τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ὡραιότης ἀγροῦ μετ᾿ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν. Ἐὰν πεινάσω, οὐ μή σοι εἴπω· ἐμὴ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ οἰκουμένη καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Μὴ φάγωμαι κρέα ταύρων. ἢ αἷμα τράγων πίωμαι; Θῦσον τῷ θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως. καὶ ἀπόδος τῷ ὑψίστῳ τὰς εὐχάς σου· καὶ ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με. Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἵνα τί σὺ ἐκδιηγῇ τὰ δικαιώματά μου, καὶ ἀναλαμβάνεις τὴν διαθήκην μου διὰ στόματός σου; Σὺ δὲ ἐμίσησας παιδείαν καὶ ἐξέβαλες τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω. Εἰ ἐθεώρεις κλέπτην, συνέτρεχες αὐτῷ, καὶ μετὰ μοιχοῦ τὴν μερίδα σου ἐτίθεις. Τὸ στόμα σου ἐπλεόνασε κακίαν, καὶ ἡ γλῶσσά σου περιέπλεκε δολιότητας. Καθήμενος κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου κατελάλεις, καὶ κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς μητρός σου ἐτίθεις σκάνδαλον. Ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα· ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος. Ἐλέγξω σε καὶ παραστήσω κατὰ πρόσωπόν σου τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου. Σύνετε δὴ ταῦτα οἱ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι τοῦ θεοῦ, μήποτε ἁρπάσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ᾖ ὁ ῥυόμενος. Θυσία αἰνέσεως δοξάσει με, καὶ ἐκεὶ ὁδός, ἥν δείξω αὐτῷ τὸ σωτήριόν μου . Οὔτε οὖν θυσίας παρ᾿ ὑμῶν λαμβάνει, οὔτε ὡς ἐνδεὴς τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐνετείλατο ποιεῖν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὑμῶν. Καὶ γὰρ τὸν ναὸν τὸν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπικληθέντα οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεὴς ὢν ὡμολόγησεν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ἢ αὐλήν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅπως καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο προσέχοντες αὐτῷ μὴ εἰδωλολατρῆτε. Καὶ ὅτι τοῦτό ἐστιν, Ἡσαΐας λέγει· Ποῖον οἶκον ᾠκοδομήσατέ μοι; λέγει κύριος. Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, καὶ ἡ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου .
pass_a_gloss: And that because of the sins of your people and because of the idolatries, but not because of being in need of such offerings, He commanded these things to be done similarly. Listen to how He speaks about these things through Amos, one of the twelve, crying out: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord. Why is this day of the Lord to you? And it is darkness and not light. Just as when a man escapes from the face of a lion, and a bear meets him, and he enters his house and leans his hands on the wall, and a snake bites him. Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light, and gloom without its brightness? I have hated, I have rejected your festivals, and I will not smell in your gatherings. For if you bring me your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look at the savior of your appearances. Turn away from me the multitude of your songs and psalms; I will not hear your instruments. And justice will roll down like water, and righteousness like an uncontrollable stream. Did you not bring me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness, house of Israel? says the Lord. And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the types which you made for yourselves. And I will exile you beyond Damascus, says the Lord; the God, the Almighty, is His name. Woe to those who waste Zion and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria. Those who are named among the leaders have rebelled against the powers of the nations; the house of Israel has entered among them. Pass through all of you into Chalane, and see, and go from there to Amath the great, and go down from there to Geth of the Philistines, the strongest of all these kingdoms, if their borders are greater than your borders. Those who come on an evil day, those who approach and touch false sabbaths, those who sleep on ivory beds and waste on their couches, those who eat lambs from the flocks and calves from the midst of the cattle, fat ones, those who strike the strings of instruments, as if they were standing and not fleeing, those who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the first myrrh, and they do not suffer anything at the crushing of Joseph. Therefore, now they will be captives from the beginning of the rulers of those being exiled, and the dwelling of the wicked will be overturned, and the noise of horses will be taken away from Ephraim. And again through Jeremiah: Gather your flesh and your sacrifices and eat, for I did not command your fathers about sacrifices or drink offerings on the day I took their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. And again through David in the forty-ninth psalm, He says thus: God of gods, the Lord spoke, and He called the earth from the rising of the sun to the setting. From Zion is the beauty of His goodness. God will come openly, our God, and He will not be silent; fire will burn before Him, and a great storm will be around Him. He will call heaven above and the earth to judge His people. Gather to Him His holy ones, those who make His covenant with sacrifices. And the heavens will declare His righteousness, for God is a judge. Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, I am. I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices, but your burnt offerings are always before me. I will not accept from your house bulls or from your flocks goats, for all the animals of the field are mine, cattle in the mountains and oxen; I know all the birds of the heaven, and the beauty of the field is with me. If I am hungry, I will not tell you; for the world is mine, and its fullness. Will I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God, and pay your vows to the Most High. And call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me. But to the sinner, God said: Why do you recite my righteousness, and take up my covenant with your mouth? You have hated discipline and cast my words behind your back. If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you placed your portion with an adulterer. Your mouth was full of evil, and your tongue was entwined with deceit. Sitting against your brother, you spoke against him, and against the son of your mother, you placed a stumbling block. You did these things, and I was silent; you thought that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face. Understand these things, you who forget God, lest He seize, and there will be no one to deliver. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there I will show him my salvation. He does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command to do this because He was in need, but because of your sins. For He did not acknowledge the temple in Jerusalem, which was called by His name, as His house or court, because He was in need, but so that you, paying attention to this, would not idolize. And that this is so, Isaiah says: What house did you build for me? says the Lord. The heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet.

The passage quotes Jeremiah 7:21-22, which speaks about the rejection of sacrifices and the importance of obedience.
The passage quotes Psalm 49, which speaks about the beauty of God's goodness and the importance of sacrifice and obedience.

pass_b_english: He gave these commands not because He needed such offerings, but because of your people's sins and their idolatry. Listen to how He addresses this through Amos, one of the twelve prophets, who cries out: Woe to you who long for the day of the Lord! Why do you want it? That day will be darkness, not light (Amos 5:18-20). It will be like a man who escapes a lion only to meet a bear, or who enters his house and leans his hand on the wall only to be bitten by a snake. The day of the Lord is darkness, not light, utter gloom without a ray of brightness. "I hate, I despise your religious festivals; your assemblies are a stench to me," He says. "Even though you bring me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. I will not even look at your peace offerings. Take away the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps. But let justice roll on like a river, righteousness like a never-failing stream!" Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings those forty years in the wilderness, people of Israel? says the Lord. You have lifted up the shrine of your king, the pedestal of your idols, the star of your god — which you made for yourselves. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is God Almighty (Amos 5:21-27). Woe to you who are complacent in Zion, and to you who feel secure on Mount Samaria! You notable men of the foremost nation, to whom the people of Israel come! Go to Kalneh and look at it; go from there to great Hamath, and then go down to Gath in Philistia. Are they better off than your two kingdoms? Is their land larger than yours? You put off the day of disaster and bring near a reign of terror. You lie on beds adorned with ivory and lounge on your couches. You dine on choice lambs and fattened calves. You strum away on your harps like David and improvise on musical instruments. You drink wine by the bowlful and use the finest lotions, but you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph. Therefore you will be among the first to go into exile; your feasting and lounging will end (Amos 6:1-7).

Again He speaks through Jeremiah: "Go ahead, add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves! For when I brought your ancestors out of Egypt and spoke to them, I did not just give them commands about burnt offerings and sacrifices" (Jeremiah 7:21-22). And again through David in the fiftieth psalm: "The Mighty One, God, the Lord, speaks and summons the earth from the rising of the sun to where it sets. From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth. Our God comes and will not be silent; a fire devours before Him, and around Him a tempest rages. He summons the heavens above, and the earth, that He may judge His people: 'Gather to Me this consecrated people, who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.' And the heavens proclaim His righteousness, for He is a God of justice" (Psalm 50:1-6). "Listen, My people, and I will speak; I will testify against you, Israel: I am God, your God. I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices or your burnt offerings, which are ever before Me. I have no need of a bull from your stall or of goats from your pens, for every animal of the forest is Mine, and the cattle on a thousand hills. I know every bird in the mountains, and the insects in the fields are Mine. If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and all that is in it. Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Sacrifice thank offerings to God, fulfill your vows to the Most High, and call on Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me" (Psalm 50:7-15).

But to the wicked person, God says: "What right have you to recite My laws or take My covenant on your lips? You hate My instruction and cast My words behind you. When you see a thief, you join with him; you throw in your lot with adulterers. You use your mouth for evil and harness your tongue to deceit. You sit and testify against your brother and slander your own mother's son. When you did these things and I kept silent, you thought I was exactly like you. But I now arraign you and set My accusations before you. Consider this, you who forget God, or I will tear you to pieces, with no one to rescue you: Those who sacrifice thank offerings honor Me, and to the blameless I will show My salvation" (Psalm 50:16-23).

So He does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command them because He was in need, but because of your sins. Even the temple in Jerusalem, which bears His name, He did not acknowledge as His house or dwelling because He needed one, but so that by fixing your attention on it you would not turn to idols. That this is so, Isaiah declares: "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool. Where is the house you will build for Me?" says the Lord (Isaiah 66:1).

review.notes: Pass B fails to translate the entire source; it omits a significant portion of the Greek text starting from 'Οὐαὶ οἱ κατασπαταλῶντες Σιὼν...' through to the end of the Amos/Jeremiah/David citations, and specifically fails to translate the section regarding the 'sinners' and the 'sacrifice of praise' (from 'Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός...' to '...δοξάσεις με'). Pass B is a partial summary/paraphrase rather than a translation of the whole chapter. Additionally, Pass B contains a scripture citation error: it identifies the Davidic psalm as 'the fiftieth psalm' (Psalm 50) in the text, whereas the Greek explicitly says 'τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ' (the forty-ninth psalm). While the note acknowledges the LXX numbering, the translation of the text itself should reflect the Greek provided.
reasons: Pass B is incomplete, omitting large sections of the Greek text (e.g., 'Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός...' through '...δοξάσεις με' and parts of the Amos section).
